landmark_cases.title: Wi-LAN, Inc. v. Apple Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Provides the Federal Circuit’s articulation of standards of review in patent jury cases, including de novo review of JMOL under regional circuit law (here, the Fifth Circuit) and claim-construction review, which frame the court’s reversal of the infringement verdict.

landmark_cases.title: Apple Inc. v. Wi-LAN Inc.
landmark_cases.reason: Restates the substantial-evidence standard governing jury infringement findings, central to determining that the record did not support the verdict here.

landmark_cases.title: Johns Hopkins University v. Datascope Corp.
landmark_cases.reason: Addresses how self-contradictory expert testimony cannot sustain a jury verdict, a key doctrinal point used to find insufficient evidence of infringement.

landmark_cases.title: Continental Circuits LLC v. Intel Corp.
landmark_cases.reason: Explains the high bar for prosecution disclaimer or disavowal—requiring clear and unambiguous statements—used to reject the argument that amendments limited the claims to three unique signals.
